newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slides to lowest since Apr 10 on stops.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slides to lowest since Apr 10 on stops.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed sharply lower across the board after a wave of fund and speculator sell-stops in the afternoon pushed July down more than 4.5 percent to the lowest level since April 10.

May ended at its session low, down 49 stg at 973 stg per tonne. July dropped 47 to 1,002, slightly off its daily low of 1,000. Turnover tallied 13,433 contracts, with July's 7,465 lots leading. May was second most active with 2,950 contracts changing hands followed by September's 1,119. All other contracts traded fewer than 1,000.
After a dull morning dominated by May/July rollovers before first notice day on May 1, futures ended the morning little changed.

But in the afternoon, the market tested the downside, pressing July through initial support at 1,040 to trigger the first round of sell-stops. Further sell-stops were hit as July fell through support at 1,030 and trendline support near 1,019 to 1,020.
Speculative liquidation and fund sales also pressured CSCE cocoa, with July puncturing support at $1,440 and a crucial double-bottom support level made in April at $1,410.

Some traders speculated that sterling's strength helped provoke the freefall. Sterling added to the one pfennig-gain against the mark made during North American trading hours on Monday. Sterling also broke resistance at $1.63 during European trading on Tuesday.
Despite the steep losses, traders noted that July stopped right on old support at 1,000 and did not come close to next support between 990 and 980, the April 9 low.

If cocoa manages to hold those key levels for the next few sessions, prices may be able to drift higher again, they said. But they said Tuesday's afternoon freefall may have seriously damaged cocoa's near-term charts, particularly because volume is expected to lighten before a three-day holiday weekend in the UK.
Markets here are closed on Monday for a bank holiday.
In options, no July contracts changed hands.
